model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on risk-weighted-asset growth

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E net operating income before impairment allowances, HK$ m: H1 2026 actual 39,903 (interim line 32; H1 2025 restated 40,137) + H2 2026E ~38,300 (H2 2025 restated 37,095, interim line 257, x ~1.03 on +6% H1 loan growth and adjusted NIM 1.57% (+3bp YoY), partly offset by weaker net trading gain). FY2025 actual 77,019 (AR line 742), FY2024 71,253. Revenue = NII + net fees + net trading + insurance and other, net of insurance claims: the Group's own 'net operating income before impairment allowances' line.
inputs.share_count_basis: 10,572,780,266 ordinary shares in issue (FY2025 AR line 5518; unchanged since the 2002 IPO). One class; no share-option or share-award scheme dilutes it; no buybacks (ShareRepurchases 0 every period). Held FLAT. The HK$10.5bn 2026-2028 additional-return programme is being delivered as special dividends (HK$0.2388/sh for 2026), not buybacks.
inputs.debt_cash_note: Bank: customer deposits (HK$3.04tn at 30 Jun 2026), interbank and subordinated liabilities (HK$79.4bn, Tier 2 capital) are operating funding and regulatory capital; cash and central-bank balances (HK$668.6bn) are liquidity, not surplus. Net debt is zero by construction on the FCFE route; nothing is bridged after the flows. The CSV's total_debt (HK$96.8bn) and cash are NOT used.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E FCFE: profit to ordinary shareholders ~42.1bn (PBT ~51.0bn = H1 actual 28,772 + H2E ~22,300; less tax and NCI at 17.5%) LESS capital retained to fund RWA growth at a 22% marginal CET1 requirement (RWA 1,231,680 FY2025 -> ~1,340,000 FY2026E: 108,320 x 22% = 23.8bn). FY2026 is the high-retention year (H1 RWA +6.3% on business growth). Reported OCF - capex (FY2025 -87,083 - 1,505; FY2023 +197,117) is deposit/interbank flow noise and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: no share-based payment line in the cash flow statement FY2017-FY2025; StockBasedComp 0 and EquityAwardTaxes 0 in the CSV every period; staff remuneration is cash (deferred variable pay). House and street bases coincide; band_position is degenerate (null).
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z HKEX regular close (Friday); valuation dated Sunday 2026-10-18
inputs.cet1_anchor: CET1 ratio 23.80% on RWA HK$1,309,167m at 30 Jun 2026 (interim lines 787-789); 24.01% on 1,231,680m at FY2025 (CET1 capital 295,716m) and 20.02% on 1,331,828m at FY2024 (AR lines 1290-1301). The FY2025 jump is the Basel III final reform package (effective 1 Jan 2025) cutting credit and operational RWAs 7.5%, not retained earnings. Total capital ratio 25.71% H1 2026.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single HKD cost of equity 9.5% in every scenario (risk is charged once, through the scenario weights and the bear drivers, not by moving the discount rate). Built in the flows' own currency: the HKD is pegged to the USD, so HKD long rates track UST; risk-free ~4.0% (ASSUMPTION: 10Y HKGB/UST range 3.6-4.4% through 2025-26, not fetched) + beta ~0.85 x mature-market ERP 5.5% = ~8.7%, plus ~0.8pt for risks the beta does not capture for a minority holder: ~66% control by state-owned Bank of China (strategy set for group/national priorities, no buyback lever), US-China sanctions/geopolitical spillover onto a Chinese-state-bank subsidiary that is Hong Kong's RMB clearing bank, and Hong Kong single-market concentration (~75% of loans) into a weak commercial-property cycle. A point below the 10.5% used for 0998.HK (CNY, joint-stock bank with a 9.4% CET1): BOCHK's CET1 is 23.8%, cost-to-income 22.5-23.6% and its rates are HKD/USD, but the HKD risk-free is ~2pt higher than CNY, so the equity risk premium charged here (~5.5pt) is LOWER than on 0998.HK (~8.7pt), which is the intended differential for the strongest-capitalised bank in the HK set. Hurdle for entry price is the house 15%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: IFRS 16 right-of-use depreciation and lease-liability interest (lease liabilities ~HK$1.7bn FY2025, AR line 10638) sit inside operating expenses, i.e. inside the pre-tax margin. lease_cost_pct_path is zero so the charge is not taken twice; nothing is deducted as debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the 'cash_tax_rate' deduction: the margin is calibrated to PROFIT BEFORE TAX (after credit impairment), and the deduction covers income tax (FY2025 ETR 15.2%, AR line 12114; FY2024 16.3%) plus profit attributable to non-controlling interests (FY2025 1,068m = 2.2% of PBT, mainly the minority in BOC Life/Nanyang-era subsidiaries). FY2025: (48,574 - 40,121) / 48,574 = 17.4%; H1 2026: (28,772 - 23,739) / 28,772 = 17.5%. No AT1 is outstanding: the US$3bn AT1 (HK$23,476m 'other equity instruments') was redeemed in 2023 and no distribution has been paid on other equity instruments since FY2023 (FY2024 AR cash flow line 6374), so nothing else sits between PBT and ordinary profit. NCI equity is NOT deducted again in a bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (0998.HK, 2016.HK, 1658.HK, HSBC, LYG, WF, BMO, NAB.AX); residual income on tangible book is the equivalent answer when retention is tied to the capital ratio, and the implied terminal P/B is reported as the cross-check. First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. Not an owner-FCF DCF: deposits are operating funding, OCF swings from -268.7bn (FY2019) to +266.3bn (FY2018), net debt is zero by construction. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = net operating income before impairment allowances; ebitda_margin = pre-tax profit margin (after credit impairment, which is the real cost of a bank); sbc, D&A, leases and working capital zero; cash_tax_rate = income tax + NCI, so EBIT x (1 - rate) = profit attributable to equity holders; capex = equity retained to fund RWA growth at a marginal CET1 requirement (g_RWA x CET1 x prior-year RWA, as % of revenue), so FCF = FCFE = distributable earnings. EXCESS CAPITAL: BOCHK runs CET1 at 23.8% against a regulatory floor (4.5% + 2.5% conservation buffer + D-SIB surcharge + HK countercyclical buffer) of roughly 9-10% and peers (HSBC group target 14.5-15.5%). Only the flow is valued: the marginal 22% (base) / 20% (bull) requirement releases a little capital as the ratio drifts down, but the ~HK$70-100bn stock surplus above a 16-18% ratio is NOT added as an equity_bridge item. Reason: management has given no CET1 target, the parent-controlled bank has historically held 17-20% even pre-Basel-reform, and the HK$10.5bn 2026-28 programme (~HK$3.5bn/yr) fits inside the modelled FCFE (FY2027E base FCFE ~HK$28.5bn vs ~HK$25bn of ordinary dividends at a ~58-60% payout), so bridging it would double-count. A formal CET1 target or a buyback would be the evidence to add surplus capital (~HK$7-9/share at 16-18%). KEY CHECKS: FY2027E base ROE ~12% on ~HK$365bn equity vs H1 2026 annualised 13.18%; price 50.15 = ~1.47x H1 2026 BVPS (~HK$34.1) and ~13.2x FY2025 EPS 3.795; dividend yield ~4.2% (FY2025 DPS 2.125) plus the 0.2388 special. QUALITATIVE: 2388.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-18) read; guidance is qualitative (no NIM/loan growth target), H1 2026 attributable profit +7.1%, credit impairment down YoY (2,472 vs 3,318), net trading gain down ~HK$5.4bn YoY, CRE Stage-2 loans HK$63.6bn at FY2025. Valuation date is 9.5 months into FY2026, so FY2026E is fy0 (not discounted) and the first discounted flow is FY2027; the FY2025 final dividend (May 2026), the 2026 interims and the 2026 special (record date mid-September 2026; the quote is ex) are paid out of fy0 and not double-counted.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.3% is >30% below revenue (7.2%) and EPS (8.7%) 5yr CAGRs. Cause: FY2020 base is a COVID/rate-trough year (NIM collapse) and FY2023-25 revenue rode the HIBOR cycle (NII 31.9bn FY2021 -> 52.9bn FY2025); equity grew slower because payout is 50-56% and the US$3bn AT1 (HK$23.5bn) was redeemed in 2023 (total equity fell FY2022-23). The 3-5% equity/BVPS pace is the better guide to sustainable growth; the drivers use 4% base revenue growth.
historical_growth.notes: FY2020-FY2025 annuals, HK$ m, CSV. Revenue FY2020 54,474 / FY2022 54,215 / FY2025 77,019; EPS 2.505 / 2.454 / 3.795; shareholders' equity 290,302 / 299,788 / 358,528. Shares flat at 10,572.78m, so net income CAGR = EPS CAGR. FCF CAGRs are null: reported OCF - capex is not a meaningful bank series (negative in FY2019, FY2022, FY2025) and SBC is zero, so there is no owner-FCF series to compound.

base.growth_rationale: Net operating income +4% for three years, easing to 3%: deposits growing ~8%/yr (2.71tn FY2024 -> 3.04tn H1 2026) and loans +6% in H1 2026 after three flat years, adjusted NIM stabilised at ~1.57% (H1 2026, +3bp YoY) with HIBOR rebounding, fee income recovering with HK IPO/wealth activity and the BOCI Private Bank acquisition, against a volatile net trading line (down ~5.4bn YoY in H1 2026). Below the 7.2% 5yr revenue CAGR, which was inflated by the 2022-24 rate cycle; in line with nominal HK GDP plus Southeast Asia/GBA share gains.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin after credit impairment. FY2021 61.2%, FY2022 61.2%, FY2023 62.5%, FY2024 65.6%, FY2025 63.1% (impairment 8,294 = 10.8% of revenue on CRE downgrades), H1 2026 72.1% (includes investment-property fair-value gains, impairment only 6.2%); FY2026E ~65%. Base holds 64.5%: cost-to-income ~24% (22.5% H1 2026, staff and tech costs growing ~3-5%), credit impairment ~8% of revenue (~0.33% of loans vs 0.13-0.16% FY2018-22 and 0.49% FY2025, i.e. CRE stress easing but not gone), small negative other items.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to fund RWA growth at a 22% marginal CET1 requirement (slightly below the 23.8% H1 2026 ratio, consistent with the 'orderly increase in payout' and the 2026-28 additional-returns programme drifting the ratio down) on RWA growth of 5.0, 5.0, 4.5, 4.5, 4.0, 4.0, 3.5, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0% from FY2026E RWA ~HK$1,340bn (FY2025 1,231.7bn, H1 2026 1,309.2bn). Retention / revenue: 0.05 x 0.22 x 1,340,000 / 81,328 = 18.1% in FY2027, falling to 11.6% as RWA growth converges on terminal growth. Terminal RWA ~HK$1,983bn; terminal ROE ~11-12%.
base.tax_rationale: HK profits tax 16.5%; ETR 15.2% FY2025 / 16.3% FY2024 / 14.8% FY2023 (tax-exempt and offshore income) + NCI ~2.2% of PBT = 17.5% (FY2025 actual 17.4%, H1 2026 17.5%), held flat. No AT1 coupons outstanding.
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 9.5% - 3.0% = ~15.8x; the 18x cap does not bind. Terminal growth 3% = long-run nominal HKD growth (peg-anchored inflation ~2% + real ~1-1.5%) and equals the terminal RWA growth, so retention and growth are internally consistent.
base.narrative: Steady-state BOCHK: NIM holds ~1.55%, loans and RWA grow 4-5% with GBA and Southeast Asia, CRE impairments ease from the FY2025 peak to ~0.33% of loans, cost-to-income ~24%, payout drifts up to ~60% with the 2026-28 programme delivered out of FCFE.

bull.growth_rationale: HIBOR stays higher for longer (NIM back toward 1.6%), RMB internationalisation and Southeast Asia lift loan growth to 5-6%, wealth/private banking and HK IPO cycle compound fee income at high single digits.
bull.margin_rationale: CRE impairments normalise to ~0.2% of loans (FY2018-22 level 0.13-0.16%), cost-to-income stays ~23%: margin rises to 67% (FY2024 was 65.6% with impairment 5.1bn).
bull.capex_rationale: RWA growth 5.5, 5.5, 5, 5, 4.5, 4, 4, 3.5, 3.5, 3.5% at a 20% marginal CET1 requirement (management lets the ratio drift toward ~20% as capital returns rise). Faster balance-sheet growth absorbs most of the lower requirement, so retention/revenue is close to base.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon 9.5% - 3.5% = ~17.3x; the 18x cap does not bind.
bull.narrative: BOCHK as the RMB/GBA/ASEAN super-connector: rates stay supportive, loan growth re-accelerates, CRE losses run off, margins expand and surplus capital is returned faster. Surplus CET1 stock (~HK$7-9/share above a 16-18% ratio) is still NOT credited.

bear.growth_rationale: Renewed Fed cutting pulls HIBOR and NIM down (FY2025 NIM fell 6bp to 1.40% reported), net trading gain mean-reverts lower (already -5.4bn YoY in H1 2026), HK loan demand stays subdued; revenue near flat in FY2027 then ~2.5-3%.
bear.margin_rationale: CRE Stage-2 book (HK$63.6bn FY2025) migrates to Stage 3: impairment ~13-14% of revenue (~0.6% of loans, above FY2025's 0.49%) for two years with negative operating leverage, then a 61% margin, the FY2020-22 trough level (61.2-61.6%).
bear.capex_rationale: RWA growth 4, 4, 3.5, 3.5, 3, 3, 2.5% ... at the full 23.8% current CET1 ratio (capital held against CRE losses and regulatory/geopolitical uncertainty; no release). RWA keeps growing faster than revenue as risk density rises, so retention bites harder relative to earnings.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon 9.5% - 2.5% = ~14.6x; the cap does not bind.
bear.narrative: HK property and rate down-cycle together: NIM compresses, CRE losses peak in 2027-28, trading income normalises lower, CET1 is held at ~24% and the payout rise stalls. Not a solvency case: CET1 is 2.5x the regulatory floor.

scenario_narratives.base: NIM holds ~1.55%, loans/RWA grow 4-5% on GBA and Southeast Asia, CRE impairments ease from the FY2025 peak, cost-to-income ~24%, ROE ~12%, payout drifts to ~60% with the HK$10.5bn 2026-28 programme funded from FCFE.
scenario_narratives.bull: Higher-for-longer HIBOR, RMB internationalisation and wealth/IPO fees lift revenue growth to ~5.5%, CRE losses run off to pre-2023 levels (margin 67%), and capital is returned faster at a 20% marginal CET1.
scenario_narratives.bear: Fed cuts compress NIM, trading income mean-reverts, CRE Stage-2 loans migrate to Stage 3 (impairment ~0.6% of loans for two years), revenue flat in FY2027, CET1 held at 23.8% with no release.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the bear-heavy 35% used for 0998.HK: BOCHK's CET1 (23.8%) is 2.5x its floor, cost-to-income is the best in the HK set and H1 2026 impairments fell YoY, so the downside is an earnings case, not a capital case. Bear is not trimmed below 25% because CRE Stage-2 exposure doubled in FY2025, a meaningful share of profit is volatile trading income, and NIM is set by the Fed via the peg. Bull is capped at 25% because the parent-controlled bank has given no CET1 target and surplus capital release is discretionary.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value BOCHK on the equity cash it can distribute: profit to ordinary shareholders less the CET1 needed to grow its risk-weighted assets, discounted at a HKD cost of equity of 9.5%. Deposits are funding, not debt; net debt is zero. The large surplus capital stock is treated as optionality, not value, until management commits to a CET1 target or buybacks.
key_risks_to_valuation: Commercial real estate: Stage-2 loans HK$63.6bn at FY2025 (+29.3bn); a migration to Stage 3 is the bear case's margin cut
NIM and HKD rates follow the Fed via the peg; each ~5bp of NIM is roughly HK$2bn of pre-tax profit on ~HK$3.8tn of interest-earning assets
Net trading gain (HK$16.8bn FY2025, >30% of PBT by management's attribution) is volatile and partly FX-swap funding arbitrage
Surplus capital (~HK$7-9/share above a 16-18% CET1) is not valued; a formal target or buyback would lift value, a regulatory change or parent-driven use would not
Geopolitical/sanctions spillover from the Bank of China parent; minority holders' limited influence over a ~66% controlling shareholder
Cost of equity: at 8.5% the base value rises ~16% (18x terminal cap binds above 3% growth); at 10.5% it falls ~14% (see sensitivity grid)
